primary.provenance_note: Published PawBench rows predate the current September 2026 canonical review refs; later observations must preserve the published harness versions and historical-lineage relation explicitly.
primary.grading_note: PawBench v1.0 mixes automated, LLM-judge and hybrid grading; grading mode remains part of benchmark identity.

primary_candidate.scope_note: Software-engineering specific; do not promote this result to universal S1 capability.

additional_evidence.scope_note: Software-engineering and terminal-task scope; useful for broad canonical harness overlap and cost/cache/time robustness checks.

reviewed_direct_families.blocking_reason: The coordination organization and protocol are benchmark-scaffolded; published comparisons do not yet isolate native S2 implementations across canonical harnesses under a matched model.
The benchmark supplies the management tool surface, worker pool and team organization; published comparison varies the main-agent model rather than native S3 implementations of canonical harnesses.
The complementary audit function is supplied by the external TrueCall layer, so wrapped harness results cannot be attributed as native S3* capability of the canonical harness.

S4.blocking_reason: Current direct families evaluate benchmark-defined or composed adaptation loops rather than matched native S4 implementations across canonical harnesses.
S4.frozen_repertoire_note: Ordinary S4 evaluation may use the current S4 repertoire to adapt other organizational capability; persistent improvement of S4's own decision/feedback repertoire belongs to the separate self-organizing-S evidence class.

S5.blocking_reason: No reviewed benchmark family currently provides direct legitimate ultimate-policy/identity authority, actual adjudication or revision, and return of the newly decided policy into subsequent operation.

raw_metric_rule: Do not duplicate numeric benchmark results in this selection record. Store each result once in the shared raw observation layer and reference it from function/domain projections.
replacement_rule: A stronger benchmark may replace a primary baseline without deleting historical observations or secondary/domain evidence.
